pages.title: Authentication
pages.markdown:
# Authentication

> Fuente: https://developers.activecollab.com/api-documentation/v1/authentication.html

Token can be obtained from the ActiveCollab interface, or programmatically, using /issue-token command. To demonstrate, lets create a new user account with a known password:

**`POST /users`** → HTTP 200

Payload:
```json
{
    "type": "Member",
    "email": "member@activecollab.com",
    "password": "Easy to remember, hard to guess"
}
```

Respuesta:
```json
{
    "single": {
        "id": 2,
        "class": "Member",
        "url_path": "\/users\/2",
        "is_archived": false,
        "is_trashed": false,
        "trashed_on": null,
        "trashed_by_id": 0,
        "created_on": 1430163964,
        "created_by_id": 1,
        "updated_on": 1430163964,
        "updated_by_id": 1,
        "language_id": 0,
        "first_name": "Member",
        "last_name": null,
        "display_name": "member",
        "short_display_name": "member",
        "email": "member@activecollab.com",
        "additional_email_addresses": [],
        "is_pending_activation": false,
        "avatar_url": "http:\/\/feather.dev\/proxy.php?proxy=avatar&module=system&v=current&b=DEV&user_id=2&size=--SIZE--&timestamp=1430163964",
        "custom_permissions": [],
        "company_id": 0,
        "title": null,
        "phone": null,
        "im_type": null,
        "im_handle": null,
        "note": null
    }
... (1 líneas más)
```

Now, lets issue a token:

**`POST /issue-token`** → HTTP 200

Payload:
```json
{
    "username": "member@activecollab.com",
    "password": "Easy to remember, hard to guess",
    "client_name": "My Awesome App",
    "client_vendor": "ACME Inc"
}
```

Respuesta:
```json
{
    "is_ok": true,
    "token": "2-6zmW8dnKpHqPLwVk2f3LMrTfVxAiJU1DibofeCPt"
}
```

That's it, we just got a token that we can store and reuse to authenticate this user in future requests. In case of error, ActiveCollab will return error dump:

**`POST /issue-token`** → HTTP 500

Payload:
```json
{
    "username": "member@activecollab.com",
    "password": "Invalid Password",
    "client_name": "My Awesome App",
    "client_vendor": "ACME Inc"
}
```

Respuesta:
```json
{
    "type": "ApiSubscriptionError",
    "message": "Invalid password",
    "file": "\/var\/www\/angie.back\/frameworks\/authentication\/models\/api_subscriptions\/FwApiSubscriptions.class.php",
    "line": 101,
    "trace": "#0 \/var\/www\/angie.back\/frameworks\/authentication\/controllers\/FwUserSessionController.class.php(71): FwApiSubscriptions::subscribe('member@activeco...', 'Invalid Passwor...', 'My Awesome App', 'ACME Inc', false)\n#1 \/var\/www\/angie.back\/src\/Angie\/Controller.php(42): FwUserSessionController->issue_token(Object(Owner))\n#2 \/var\/www\/angie.back\/classes\/application\/AngieApplicationAdapter.class.php(243): Angie\\Controller->executeAction('issue_token')\n#3 \/var\/www\/angie.back\/classes\/application\/AngieApplication.class.php(839): AngieApplicationAdapter->handleHttpRequest('issue-token', '')\n#4 \/var\/www\/activecollab.back\/instance\/public\/api.php(19): AngieApplication::handleHttpRequest()\n#5 {main}",
    "previous": null,
    "code": 3
}
```

**`POST /issue-token`** → HTTP 500

Payload:
```json
{
    "username": "unknown-user@activecollab.com",
    "password": "Easy to remember, hard to guess",
    "client_name": "My Awesome App",
    "client_vendor": "ACME Inc"
}
```

Respuesta:
```json
{
    "type": "ApiSubscriptionError",
    "message": "User does not exist",
    "file": "\/var\/www\/angie.back\/frameworks\/authentication\/models\/api_subscriptions\/FwApiSubscriptions.class.php",
    "line": 104,
    "trace": "#0 \/var\/www\/angie.back\/frameworks\/authentication\/controllers\/FwUserSessionController.class.php(71): FwApiSubscriptions::subscribe('unknown-user@ac...', 'Easy to remembe...', 'My Awesome App', 'ACME Inc', false)\n#1 \/var\/www\/angie.back\/src\/Angie\/Controller.php(42): FwUserSessionController->issue_token(Object(Owner))\n#2 \/var\/www\/angie.back\/classes\/application\/AngieApplicationAdapter.class.php(243): Angie\\Controller->executeAction('issue_token')\n#3 \/var\/www\/angie.back\/classes\/application\/AngieApplication.class.php(839): AngieApplicationAdapter->handleHttpRequest('issue-token', '')\n#4 \/var\/www\/activecollab.back\/instance\/public\/api.php(19): AngieApplication::handleHttpRequest()\n#5 {main}",
    "previous": null,
    "code": 2
}
```

**`PUT /move-to-archive/user/2`** → HTTP 200

Respuesta:
```json

        "display_name": "member",

        "custom_permissions": [],

        "title": null,
        "phone": null,
        "im_type": null,
        "im_handle": null,
        "note": null
    }
... (1 líneas más)
```

**`POST /issue-token`** → HTTP 500

Payload:
```json
{
    "username": "member@activecollab.com",
    "password": "Easy to remember, hard to guess",
    "client_name": "My Awesome App",
    "client_vendor": "ACME Inc"
}
```

Respuesta:
```json
{
    "type": "ApiSubscriptionError",
    "message": "User does not exist",
    "file": "\/var\/www\/angie.back\/frameworks\/authentication\/models\/api_subscriptions\/FwApiSubscriptions.class.php",
    "line": 104,
    "trace": "#0 \/var\/www\/angie.back\/frameworks\/authentication\/controllers\/FwUserSessionController.class.php(71): FwApiSubscriptions::subscribe('member@activeco...', 'Easy to remembe...', 'My Awesome App', 'ACME Inc', false)\n#1 \/var\/www\/angie.back\/src\/Angie\/Controller.php(42): FwUserSessionController->issue_token(Object(Owner))\n#2 \/var\/www\/angie.back\/classes\/application\/AngieApplicationAdapter.class.php(243): Angie\\Controller->executeAction('issue_token')\n#3 \/var\/www\/angie.back\/classes\/application\/AngieApplication.class.php(839): AngieApplicationAdapter->handleHttpRequest('issue-token', '')\n#4 \/var\/www\/activecollab.back\/instance\/public\/api.php(19): AngieApplication::handleHttpRequest()\n#5 {main}",
    "previous": null,
    "code": 2
}
```

Following error codes are provided:

- `0` - Operation failed (general error),
- `1` - Information about client application is not set,
- `2` - User does not exist or not active,
- `3` - Password is not valid,
- `4` - Issue token not allowed for the user.

pages.title: Config Options
pages.markdown:
# Config Options

> Fuente: https://developers.activecollab.com/api-documentation/v1/config-options.html

To get a list of options and their default values, simply send GET request to /config-options path and provide a comma separated list of option names:

**`GET /config-options`** → HTTP 200

Parámetros de query:
```json
{
    "names": "notifications_user_send_morning_paper,morning_paper_last_activity"
}
```

Respuesta:
```json
{
    "notifications_user_send_morning_paper": true
}
```

Notice that options that are not available via API are not listed. Only options that can be accessed via API will be returned.

To update default values, you can PUT new values:

**`PUT /config-options`** → HTTP 200

Payload:
```json
{
    "notifications_user_send_morning_paper": false,
    "morning_paper_last_activity": false
}
```

Respuesta:
```json
{
    "notifications_user_send_morning_paper": false
}
```

Protected options (like morning_paper_last_activity are ignored).

To get user specific values, send GET request to /personalized-config-options:

**`GET /personalized-config-options`** → HTTP 200

Parámetros de query:
```json
{
    "names": "notifications_user_send_morning_paper"
}
```

Respuesta:
```json
{
    "notifications_user_send_morning_paper": false
}
```

In this request, we got default value. Lets save a value just for us:

**`PUT /personalized-config-options`** → HTTP 200

Payload:
```json
{
    "notifications_user_send_morning_paper": true
}
```

Respuesta:
```json
{
    "notifications_user_send_morning_paper": true
}
```

Now, lets confirm that the default value remained the same:

**`GET /config-options`** → HTTP 200

Parámetros de query:
```json
{
    "names": "notifications_user_send_morning_paper"
}
```

Respuesta:
```json
{
    "notifications_user_send_morning_paper": false
}
```

pages.title: Info
pages.markdown:
# Info

> Fuente: https://developers.activecollab.com/api-documentation/v1/info.html

If you need to know the basic information about the application that you are communicating with (like full application name and version number), you can call /info:

**`GET /info`** → HTTP 200

Respuesta:
```json
{
    "application": "ActiveCollab",
    "version": "current"
}
```

# Initial

> Fuente: https://developers.activecollab.com/api-documentation/v1/initial.html

Personas in this Story: Default, Client.

`initial` command bundles up a lot of data that you might need when you are starting, in a single command. These collections and settings are not personalised, but global and don't change frequently. Collection itself is etagged, so it is recommended for your client to cache it and check for modifications:

**`GET /initial`** → HTTP 200

Respuesta:
```json

        "identity_name": "Application",
```

pages.title: Company Addresses

# Company Addresses

> Fuente: https://developers.activecollab.com/api-documentation/v1/invoicing/company-addresses.html

ActiveCollab offers a simple API that lets you implement auto-complete for invoice, estimate or recurring profile client. This API will provide all companies defined in the People section (except owner company), plus all companies previously used in invoices, estimates and recurring profiles that are not saved in People section.

pages.title: Note Templates
pages.markdown:
# Note Templates

> Fuente: https://developers.activecollab.com/api-documentation/v1/invoicing/invoices/note-templates.html

Invoice note templates are useful when you frequently include the same or similar note in your invoices (payment instructions, tax specific details etc). By default, ActiveCollab will not provide any template:

**`GET /invoice-note-templates`** → HTTP 200

Respuesta:
```json
[]
```

You can defined them like this:

**`POST /invoice-note-templates`** → HTTP 200

Payload:
```json
{
    "name": "Payment instructions",
    "content": "Please make payment to this account: ABC"
}
```

Respuesta:
```json
{
    "single": {
        "id": 1,
        "class": "InvoiceNoteTemplate",
        "url_path": "\/invoice-note-templates\/1",
        "name": "Payment instructions",
        "content": "Please make payment to this account: ABC",
        "is_default": false
    }
}
```

To update a template, simply send PUT command:

**`PUT /invoice-note-templates/1`** → HTTP 200

Payload:
```json
{
    "content": "Please make payment to this account: XYZ"
}
```

Respuesta:
```json
{
    "single": {
        "id": 1,
        "class": "InvoiceNoteTemplate",
        "url_path": "\/invoice-note-templates\/1",
        "name": "Payment instructions",
        "content": "Please make payment to this account: XYZ",
        "is_default": false
    }
}
```

## Default Note Template

ActiveCollab lets you set up a default note template. Default note template can save you time by automatically adding a note to all your new templates. By default, there is no default note template:

**`GET /invoice-note-templates/default`** → HTTP 404

**`PUT /invoice-note-templates/default`** → HTTP 200

Payload:
```json
{
    "invoice_note_template_id": 1
}
```

Respuesta:
```json
{
    "single": {
        "id": 1,
        "class": "InvoiceNoteTemplate",
        "url_path": "\/invoice-note-templates\/1",
        "name": "Payment instructions",
        "content": "Please make payment to this account: XYZ",
        "is_default": true
    }
}
```

To unset default note template, simply send DELETE request:

**`DELETE /invoice-note-templates/default`** → HTTP 200

## Deleting a Note Template

To delete a note template, send DELETE command to /invoice-note-templates/:invoice_note_template_id:

**`DELETE /invoice-note-templates/1`** → HTTP 200

pages.markdown:
# Tax Rates

> Fuente: https://developers.activecollab.com/api-documentation/v1/invoicing/invoices/tax-rates.html

Tax rates are used to specify taxes that will be used when creating invoices. By default, ActiveCollab ships an example tax rate:

**`GET /tax-rates`** → HTTP 200

Respuesta:
```json
[
    {
        "id": 1,
        "class": "TaxRate",
        "url_path": "\/tax-rates\/1",
        "name": "VAT",
        "percentage": 17.5,
        "is_default": false
    }
]
```

The rate is not good, so we'll adjust it:

**`PUT /tax-rates/1`** → HTTP 200

Payload:
```json
{
    "percentage": 22
}
```

Respuesta:
```json
{
    "single": {
        "id": 1,
        "class": "TaxRate",
        "url_path": "\/tax-rates\/1",
        "name": "VAT",
        "percentage": 22,
        "is_default": false
    }
}
```

Lets add two more tax rates:

**`POST /tax-rates`** → HTTP 200

Payload:
```json
{
    "name": "ADD1",
    "percentage": 5
}
```

Respuesta:
```json
{
    "single": {
        "id": 2,
        "class": "TaxRate",
        "url_path": "\/tax-rates\/2",
        "name": "ADD1",
        "percentage": 5,
        "is_default": false
    }
}
```

**`POST /tax-rates`** → HTTP 200

Payload:
```json
{
    "name": "ADD2",
    "percentage": 4.5
}
```

Respuesta:
```json
{
    "single": {
        "id": 3,
        "class": "TaxRate",
        "url_path": "\/tax-rates\/3",
        "name": "ADD2",
        "percentage": 4.5,
        "is_default": false
    }
}
```

Now we'll create a new invoice and use `VAT`, to demonstrate that used tax rates can't be updated or deleted:

**`POST /invoices`** → HTTP 200

Payload:
```json
{
    "company_id": 0,
    "company_name": "Client Company GmbH",
    "company_address": "Street Name 12\nCity",
    "number": "1\/2014",
    "items": [
        {
            "description": "First item",
            "quantity": 100,
            "unit_cost": 25
        },
        {
            "description": "Second item",
            "quantity": 250,
            "unit_cost": 13,
            "first_tax_rate_id": 2
        },
        {
            "description": "Third item",
            "quantity": 15,
            "unit_cost": 25
        }
    ]
}
```

Respuesta:
```json
{
    "single": {
        "id": 1,
        "class": "Invoice",
        "url_path": "\/invoices\/1",
        "is_trashed": false,
        "trashed_on": null,
        "trashed_by_id": 0,
        "company_id": 0,
        "company_name": "Client Company GmbH",
        "company_address": "Street Name 12\nCity",
        "note": null,
        "currency_id": 0,
        "language_id": 0,
        "discount_rate": 0,
        "subtotal": 6125,
        "subtotal_without_discount": 6125,
        "discount": 0,
        "tax": 162.5,
        "rounding_difference": 0,
        "rounded_total": 6287.5,
        "total": 6287.5,
        "paid_amount": 0,
        "balance_due": 6287.5,
        "recipients": null,
        "email_from": null,
        "email_subject": null,
        "email_body": null,
        "second_tax_is_enabled": false,
        "second_tax_is_compound": false,
... (109 líneas más)
```

Note that rate of a tax that is already used in an invoice can't be changed:

**`PUT /tax-rates/2`** → HTTP 200

Payload:
```json
{
    "percentage": 18
}
```

Respuesta:
```json
{
    "single": {
        "id": 2,
        "class": "TaxRate",
        "url_path": "\/tax-rates\/2",
        "name": "ADD1",
        "percentage": 5,
        "is_default": false
    }
}
```

ActiveCollab will not throw an error, but it will ignore the change. We recommend that you add a new tax record.

## Default Tax Rate

ActiveCollab lets you set up a tax rate that will be set as invoice it's tax rate by default. This feature is off by default:

**`GET /tax-rates/default`** → HTTP 404

**`PUT /tax-rates/default`** → HTTP 200

Payload:
```json
{
    "tax_rate_id": 1
}
```

Respuesta:
```json
{
    "single": {
        "id": 1,
        "class": "TaxRate",
        "url_path": "\/tax-rates\/1",
        "name": "VAT",
        "percentage": 22,
        "is_default": true
    }
}
```

To unset default tax rate, simply send DELETE request:

**`DELETE /tax-rates/default`** → HTTP 200

## Deleting a Tax Rate

To delete a tax rate, send DELETE command to /tax-rates/:tax_rate_id. Note that default tax rate can't be deleted:

**`PUT /tax-rates/default`** → HTTP 200

Payload:
```json
{
    "tax_rate_id": 1
}
```

Respuesta:
```json
{
    "single": {
        "id": 1,
        "class": "TaxRate",
        "url_path": "\/tax-rates\/1",
        "name": "VAT",
        "percentage": 22,
        "is_default": true
    }
}
```

**`DELETE /tax-rates/1`** → HTTP 404

Tax rates that are used in invoices can't be deleted:

**`DELETE /tax-rates/2`** → HTTP 404

Unused tax rates can be deleted:

**`DELETE /tax-rates/3`** → HTTP 200

pages.title: Gateways
pages.markdown:
# Gateways

> Fuente: https://developers.activecollab.com/api-documentation/v1/invoicing/payments/gateways.html

ActiveCollab can receive two types of payments: PayPal and creadit card payments. For PayPal payments we use `PaypalExpressCheckoutGateway`, and for credit card processing we use one of the following gateways:

- `AuthorizeGateway`
- `BrainTreeGateway`
- `PaypalDirectPayment`
- `StripeGateway`

By default, there is no payment gateway configured:

**`GET /payment-gateways`** → HTTP 200

Respuesta:
```json
{
    "paypal": null,
    "credit_card": null
}
```

## Paypal Express Checkout

and PayPal using PayPal Express Checkout:

## Stripe

Stripe is used to process credit cars. Only parameter that is required is API key. Lets configure the system to use a API for testing:

**`PUT /payment-gateways`** → HTTP 200

Payload:
```json
{
    "credit_card": {
        "type": "StripeGateway",
        "api_key": "sk_test_REDACTED"
    }
}
```

Respuesta:
```json
{
    "paypal": null,
    "credit_card": {
        "id": 1,
        "class": "StripeGateway",
        "url_path": "#",
        "is_live": false,
        "api_key": "sk_test_REDACTED"
    }
}
```

now lets try with Live mode:

**`PUT /payment-gateways`** → HTTP 200

Payload:
```json
{
    "credit_card": {
        "type": "StripeGateway",
        "api_key": "sk_live_REDACTED"
    }
}
```

Respuesta:
```json
{
    "paypal": null,
    "credit_card": {
        "id": 2,
        "class": "StripeGateway",
        "url_path": "#",
        "is_live": true,
        "api_key": "sk_live_REDACTED"
    }
}
```

## Authorize.net

To use Authorize.net, two parameters are needed: api_login_id and transaction_key. By default, system is in test mode:

**`PUT /payment-gateways`** → HTTP 200

Payload:
```json
{
    "credit_card": {
        "type": "AuthorizeGateway",
        "api_login_id": "XYZ",
        "transaction_key": "ABC"
    }
}
```

Respuesta:
```json
{
    "paypal": null,
    "credit_card": {
        "id": 3,
        "class": "AuthorizeGateway",
        "url_path": "#",
        "is_live": false,
        "api_login_id": "XYZ",
        "transaction_key": "ABC"
    }
}
```

to put the system in production mode, explicitely set is_live to true when setting up the gateway:

**`PUT /payment-gateways`** → HTTP 200

Payload:
```json
{
    "credit_card": {
        "type": "AuthorizeGateway",
        "api_login_id": "XYZ",
        "transaction_key": "ABC",
        "is_live": true
    }
}
```

Respuesta:
```json
{
    "paypal": null,
    "credit_card": {
        "id": 4,
        "class": "AuthorizeGateway",
        "url_path": "#",
        "is_live": true,
        "api_login_id": "XYZ",
        "transaction_key": "ABC"
    }
}
```

## Braintree

To configure ActiveCollab to process credit cards using Braintree, you need to provide merchant_id, public_key, private_key and merchant account ID for at least the default currency. By default, this gateway is in test mode:

**`PUT /payment-gateways`** → HTTP 200

Payload:
```json
{
    "credit_card": {
        "type": "BrainTreeGateway",
        "merchant_id": "XYZ",
        "merchant_account_ids": {
            "USD": "123",
            "EUR": "456",
            "UNKNOWN": "Unknown currency is ignored"
        },
        "public_key": "ABC",
        "private_key": "FGH"
    }
}
```

Respuesta:
```json
{
    "paypal": null,
    "credit_card": {
        "id": 5,
        "class": "BrainTreeGateway",
        "url_path": "#",
        "is_live": false,
        "merchant_id": "XYZ",
        "merchant_account_ids": {
            "EUR": "456",
            "USD": "123"
        },
        "public_key": "ABC",
        "private_key": "FGH"
    }
}
```

to put the system in production mode, explicitely set is_live to true when setting up the gateway:

**`PUT /payment-gateways`** → HTTP 200

Payload:
```json
{
    "credit_card": {
        "type": "BrainTreeGateway",
        "merchant_id": "XYZ",
        "merchant_account_ids": {
            "USD": "123",
            "EUR": "456"
        },
        "public_key": "ABC",
        "private_key": "FGH",
        "is_live": true
    }
}
```

Respuesta:
```json
{
    "paypal": null,
    "credit_card": {
        "id": 6,
        "class": "BrainTreeGateway",
        "url_path": "#",
        "is_live": true,
        "merchant_id": "XYZ",
        "merchant_account_ids": {
            "EUR": "456",
            "USD": "123"
        },
        "public_key": "ABC",
        "private_key": "FGH"
    }
}
```

## PayPal Direct Payment

PayPal can be used not just for offsite payments, but also to process credit cards. To configure ActiveCollab to process credit cards using PayPal gateway, you need to provide api_username, api_password and api_signature. By default, this gateway is in test mode:

**`PUT /payment-gateways`** → HTTP 200

Payload:
```json
{
    "credit_card": {
```

# Teams

> Fuente: https://developers.activecollab.com/api-documentation/v1/people/teams/teams.html

Teams are used to group people. By default, activeCollab ships with no teams:

**`GET /teams`** → HTTP 200

Respuesta:
```json
[]
```

To create a team, we should send a POST request to `/teams` path and include team's name and members:

**`POST /teams`** → HTTP 200

Payload:
```json
{
    "name": "Developers",
    "members": [
        1,
        2
    ]
}
```

Respuesta:
```json
{
    "single": {
        "id": 1,
        "class": "Team",
```

```json
        "class": "Team",

            2
```

# Password Recovery

> Fuente: https://developers.activecollab.com/api-documentation/v1/people/users/password-recovery.html

NOTE: Instructions on this page assume that you are using default authentication provider. If you are using custom authentication provider, double check its documentation to see if password recovery is supported and what bit of information is considered to be user's username.

To initiate password recovery, send POST request to `/password-recovery/send-code` command with valid email address:

**`POST /password-recovery/send-code`** → HTTP 200

Payload:
```json
{
    "username": "member@activecollab.com"
}
```

Respuesta:
```json
{
    "code_sent_to": "member@activecollab.com"
}
```

This works for user's alaternative addresses as well. Note that in that case, password recovery instructions are sent to user's primary email address:

**`POST /password-recovery/send-code`** → HTTP 200

Payload:
```json
{
    "username": "additional-address-for-member@activecollab.com"
}
```

Respuesta:
```json
{
    "code_sent_to": "member@activecollab.com"
}
```

**`POST /password-recovery/reset-password`** → HTTP 500

```json
{
    "user_id": 2,
    "code": "076f91da733a828adbc2",
```

# User State Changes

> Fuente: https://developers.activecollab.com/api-documentation/v1/people/users/user-state-changes.html

In activeCollab, objects usually have one of the three states:

1. Active - object is active and relevant,
2. Archived - we have done working with a particular object and system will try to keep it off sight as much as possible,
3. Trashed - object has been moved to Trash. Users can restore it from Trash if needed within 30 days from the time when it was moved to Trash.

> **Nota:** Some objects get archived automatically, and some need to be explicetly moved to archive by the user. For example, projects, task lists and tasks get archived when you complete them, but users, companies, job types etc don't.

## Working with Archive

All objects start as active, and than can be moved to trash or archive. Lets see how this work on an example of a person who temporaly left our company:

**`GET /users/2`** → HTTP 200

> Fuente: https://developers.activecollab.com/api-documentation/v1/people/users/users.html

# Validate Email Address

> Fuente: https://developers.activecollab.com/api-documentation/v1/people/users/validate-email-address.html

For the purpose of this test, we have created tree use accounts:

1. User #2 with member2@activecollab.com address - Active account
2. User #3 with member3@activecollab.com address - Archived account
3. User #4 with member4@activecollab.com address - Trashed account

To check if a given email address is available for new user accounts (handy when inviting new users), we can use `/users/check-email` command. Response of this command is an object with three fields:

1. valid_address - True if format of the input address is valid,
2. in_use - false when address is not in use. When in use, this can have one of the following `active`, `achived`, `invited` and `trashed`,
3. user_id - ID of an account that is using this address (NULL when there is no such account).

First, lets check for invalid email address:

**`GET /users/check-email?email=invalid-address`** → HTTP 200

Respuesta:
```json
{
    "valid_address": false,
    "in_use": false,
    "user_id": null
}
```

Good. Lets check for an active user account:

**`GET /users/check-email?email=member2@activecollab.com`** → HTTP 200

Respuesta:
```json
{
    "valid_address": true,
    "in_use": "active",
    "user_id": 2
}
```

via additional address:

**`GET /users/check-email?email=additional-address-for-member2@activecollab.com`** → HTTP 200

Respuesta:
```json
{
    "valid_address": true,
    "in_use": "active",
    "user_id": 2
}
```

Invite user:

**`GET /users/check-email?email=member3@activecollab.com`** → HTTP 200

Respuesta:
```json
{
    "valid_address": true,
    "in_use": "invited",
    "user_id": 3
}
```

Now lets check an archived user account:

**`GET /users/check-email?email=member4@activecollab.com`** → HTTP 200

Respuesta:
```json
{
    "valid_address": true,
    "in_use": "archived",
    "user_id": 4
}
```

And trashed account:

**`GET /users/check-email?email=member5@activecollab.com`** → HTTP 200

Respuesta:
```json
{
    "valid_address": true,
    "in_use": "trashed",
    "user_id": 5
}
```

Finally, lets check for an address that is not in use:

**`GET /users/check-email?email=not-in-use@activecollab.com`** → HTTP 200

Respuesta:
```json
{
    "valid_address": true,
    "in_use": false,
    "user_id": null
}
```

# Permissions

> Fuente: https://developers.activecollab.com/api-documentation/v1/projects/budget/permissions.html

Personas in this Story: Default, Member, ProjectManager, FinancialManager, Client.

Project budget can be set per project when time and expense tracking is enabled on that project. When enabled, ActiveCollab will provide a nice budget report which shows how much time and expenses is tracked, and how these numbers stand against set budget. In order to demonstrate how this works, we have one project defined:

**`GET /projects/1`** → HTTP 200

Respuesta:
```json

    "single": {
        "id": 1,
        "class": "Project",
        "url_path": "\/projects\/1",
        "name": "Budget test",
        "completed_on": null,
        "completed_by_id": null,
```

pages.title: Discussions
pages.markdown:
# Discussions > Fuente: https://developers.activecollab.com/api-documentation/v1/projects/elements/discussions/discussions.html To list all discussions in a project, send GET request to `/projects/:project_id/discussions` path: **`GET /projects/1/discussions`** → HTTP 200 Respuesta: ```json { "discussions": [], "comments": [] } ``` As we can see, there are no discussions in this projects. To create a new discussions, send POST request to `/projects/:project_id/discussions` path: **`POST /projects/1/discussions`** → HTTP 200 Payload: ```json { "name": "New Discussion" } ``` Respuesta: ```json { "single": { "id": 1, "class": "Discussion", "url_path": "\/projects\/1\/discussions\/1", "name": "New Discussion", "comments_count": 0, "attachments": [], "is_trashed": false, "trashed_on": null, "trashed_by_id": 0, "project_id": 1, "is_hidden_from_clients": false, "body": "", "body_formatted": "", "created_on": 1430164053, "created_by_id": 1, "updated_on": 1430164053, "updated_by_id": 1 }, "subscribers": [ 1 ], "comments": [] } ``` If we execute `/projects/:project_id/discussions` again, we'll see that we have successfully added a discussion: **`GET /projects/1/discussions`** → HTTP 200 Respuesta: ```json { "discussions": [ { "id": 1, "class": "Discussion", "url_path": "\/projects\/1\/discussions\/1", "name": "New Discussion", "comments_count": 0, "attachments": [], "is_trashed": false, "trashed_on": null, "trashed_by_id": 0, "project_id": 1, "is_hidden_from_clients": false, "body": "", "body_formatted": "", "created_on": 1430164053, "created_by_id": 1, "updated_on": 1430164053, "updated_by_id": 1 } ], "comments": [] } ``` We can also check out individual discussion details: **`GET /projects/1/discussions/1`** → HTTP 200 Respuesta: ```json { "single": { "id": 1, "class": "Discussion", "url_path": "\/projects\/1\/discussions\/1", "name": "New Discussion", "comments_count": 0, "attachments": [], "is_trashed": false, "trashed_on": null, "trashed_by_id": 0, "project_id": 1, "is_hidden_from_clients": false, "body": "", "body_formatted": "", "created_on": 1430164053, "created_by_id": 1, "updated_on": 1430164053, "updated_by_id": 1 }, "subscribers": [ 1 ], "comments": [] } ``` What is interesting about discussions is that they also list all of the other project elements that are discussed (tasks, files, and notes). Lets check: This task will not be part of the discussions response because it is not yet discussed: **`GET /projects/1/discussions`** → HTTP 200 Respuesta: ```json { "discussions": [ { "id": 1, "class": "Discussion", "url_path": "\/projects\/1\/discussions\/1", "name": "New Discussion", "comments_count": 0, "attachments": [], "is_trashed": false, "trashed_on": null, "trashed_by_id": 0, "project_id": 1, "is_hidden_from_clients": false, "body": "", "body_formatted": "", "created_on": 1430164053, "created_by_id": 1, "updated_on": 1430164053, "updated_by_id": 1 } ], "comments": [] } ``` **`POST /comments/task/1`** → HTTP 200 Payload: ```json { "body": "Comment body" } ``` Respuesta: ```json { "single": { "id": 1, "class": "Comment", "url_path": "\/comments\/1", "attachments": [], "is_trashed": false, "trashed_on": null, "trashed_by_id": 0, "parent_type": "Task", "parent_id": 1, "body": "Comment body", "body_formatted": "Comment body", "body_plain_text": "Comment body", "created_on": 1430164056, "created_by_id": 1, "updated_on": 1430164056, "updated_by_id": 1 } } ``` **`GET /projects/1/discussions`** → HTTP 200 Respuesta: ```json { "discussions": [ { "id": 1, "class": "Task", "url_path": "\/projects\/1\/tasks\/1", "name": "New Task", "assignee_id": 0, "delegated_by_id": 0, "completed_on": null, "completed_by_id": null, "is_completed": false, "comments_count": "1", "attachments": [], "labels": [], "is_trashed": false, "trashed_on": null, "trashed_by_id": 0, "project_id": 1, "is_hidden_from_clients": false, "body": "", "body_formatted": "", "created_on": 1430164054, "created_by_id": 1, "updated_on": 1430164056, "updated_by_id": 1, "task_number": 1, "task_list_id": 0, "position": 1, "is_important": false, ... (43 líneas más) ``` To update a discussion, we need to send a PUT request to the discussion URL: **`PUT /projects/1/discussions/1`** → HTTP 200 Payload: ```json { "name": "Updated Discussion Name", "body": "

> Fuente: https://developers.activecollab.com/api-documentation/v1/projects/elements/expenses/visibility.html

Personas in this Story: Default, ProjectLeader, Member, Subcontractor, Client.

This article covers visibility of expense. In broad strokes:

1. Only owners and project leader always see all expenses in a project,

To add a file to a project, first we need to upload it:

# Task Estimates

> Fuente: https://developers.activecollab.com/api-documentation/v1/projects/elements/tasks/task-estimates.html

All activeCollab tasks can have an estimate set. This is a number of hours that teams expects to spend on a task in order to complete it. To set an estimate for a task, you need to set `job_type_id` and `estimate` values. Lets see which job types we have defined:

**`GET /job-types`** → HTTP 200

Respuesta:
```json
[
    {
        "id": 1,
        "class": "JobType",
        "url_path": "\/job-types\/1",
        "name": "General",
        "is_archived": false,
        "updated_on": null,
        "is_default": true,
        "default_hourly_rate": 100
    }
]
```

Ok, we have one job type and it's name is "General". Lets create a task that we expect will take 8 and a half hours of work:

**`POST /projects/1/tasks`** → HTTP 200

Payload:
```json
{
    "name": "Task #1",
    "job_type_id": 1,
    "estimate": "8:30"
}
```

```json
        "id": 1,
```

pages.markdown:
# Task Reminders

> Fuente: https://developers.activecollab.com/api-documentation/v1/projects/elements/tasks/task-reminders.html

Personas in this Story: Default, Member.

For the purpose of this test we have created one project and one task, and invited one company member to collaborate with us. When we check task's reminders, the list will be empty:

**`GET /reminders/task/1`** → HTTP 200

Respuesta:
```json
[]
```

**`POST /reminders/task/1`** → HTTP 200

Payload:
```json
{
    "send_on": "2014\/11\/03",
    "comment": "Happy birthday"
}
```

Respuesta:
```json
{
    "single": {
        "id": 1,
        "class": "CustomReminder",
        "url_path": "\/reminders\/1",
        "parent_type": "Task",
        "parent_id": 1,
        "created_on": 1430164391,
        "created_by_id": 1,
        "comment": "Happy birthday",
        "send_on": 1414972800,
        "subscribers": []
    },
    "subscribers": []
}
```

When we try to fetch reminders now, system will return proper result:

**`GET /reminders/task/1`** → HTTP 200

Respuesta:
```json
[
    {
        "id": 1,
        "class": "CustomReminder",
        "url_path": "\/reminders\/1",
        "parent_type": "Task",
        "parent_id": 1,
        "created_on": 1430164391,
        "created_by_id": 1,
        "comment": "Happy birthday",
        "send_on": 1414972800,
        "subscribers": []
    }
]
```

Note that system returns only reminders that current user created. Reminders of other users will not be visible, and therefore Member will not be able to see the reminder created by the Owner:

**`GET /reminders/task/1`** → HTTP 200 _(como Member)_

Respuesta:
```json
[]
```

To quickly check whether task has reminders or not (and save one unneded request), simpy check `reminders` property in /projects/:project_slug/tasks/:task_id response:

**`GET /projects/1/tasks/1`** → HTTP 200

Respuesta:
```json
{
    "single": {
        "id": 1,
        "class": "Task",
        "url_path": "\/projects\/1\/tasks\/1",
        "name": "Test Task",
        "assignee_id": 0,
        "delegated_by_id": 0,
        "completed_on": null,
        "completed_by_id": null,
        "is_completed": false,

        "labels": [],

        "body_formatted": "",

        "updated_on": 1430164391,
        "updated_by_id": 1,
        "task_number": 1,
        "task_list_id": 0,
        "position": 1,
        "is_important": false,
        "due_on": null,
... (18 líneas más)
```

Reminders can only be deleted, but not updated. Because of that, we'll get 404 if we try to update a reminder:

**`PUT /reminders/1`** → HTTP 404

Respuesta:
```json
{
    "type": "Angie\\Controller\\Error\\ActionForMethodNotFound",
    "message": "Controller action reminders::delete() is not available for PUT method",
    "file": "\/var\/www\/angie.back\/classes\/application\/AngieApplicationAdapter.class.php",
    "line": 235,
    "trace": "#0 \/var\/www\/angie.back\/classes\/application\/AngieApplication.class.php(839): AngieApplicationAdapter->handleHttpRequest('reminders\/1', '')\n#1 \/var\/www\/activecollab.back\/instance\/public\/api.php(19): AngieApplication::handleHttpRequest()\n#2 {main}",
    "previous": null,
    "controller": "reminders",
    "action": "delete",
    "method": "PUT"
}
```

but correct result when we try to delete it:

**`DELETE /reminders/1`** → HTTP 200

pages.title: Job Types
pages.markdown:
# Job Types

> Fuente: https://developers.activecollab.com/api-documentation/v1/projects/elements/time-records/job-types.html

Not all work is the same, and cost the same. To address this, ActiveCollab has a concept of job type. Each tracked time records need to have a job type specified, and differnet job types can have different hourly rates (defined globally, per client and per project). By default, ActiveCollab ships with only one job type:

**`GET /job-types`** → HTTP 200

Respuesta:
```json
[
    {
        "id": 1,
        "class": "JobType",
        "url_path": "\/job-types\/1",
        "name": "General",
        "is_archived": false,
        "updated_on": null,
        "is_default": true,
        "default_hourly_rate": 100
    }
]
```

Our example company is web development consultancy, so we'll rename this job type:

**`PUT /job-types/1`** → HTTP 200

Payload:
```json
{
    "name": "Programming",
    "default_hourly_rate": 150
}
```

Respuesta:
```json
{
    "single": {
        "id": 1,
        "class": "JobType",
        "url_path": "\/job-types\/1",
        "name": "Programming",
        "is_archived": false,
        "updated_on": 1430164435,
        "is_default": true,
        "default_hourly_rate": 150
    }
}
```

and add a couple more:

**`POST /job-types`** → HTTP 200

Payload:
```json
{
    "name": "Design",
    "default_hourly_rate": 120
}
```

Respuesta:
```json
{
    "single": {
        "id": 2,
        "class": "JobType",
        "url_path": "\/job-types\/2",
        "name": "Design",
        "is_archived": false,
        "updated_on": 1430164435,
        "is_default": false,
        "default_hourly_rate": 120
    }
}
```

**`POST /job-types`** → HTTP 200

Payload:
```json
{
    "name": "SEO",
    "default_hourly_rate": 100
}
```

Respuesta:
```json
{
    "single": {
        "id": 3,
        "class": "JobType",
        "url_path": "\/job-types\/3",
        "name": "SEO",
        "is_archived": false,
        "updated_on": 1430164436,
        "is_default": false,
        "default_hourly_rate": 100
    }
}
```

**`POST /job-types`** → HTTP 200

Payload:
```json
{
    "name": "DTP",
    "default_hourly_rate": 150
}
```

Respuesta:
```json
{
    "single": {
        "id": 4,
        "class": "JobType",
        "url_path": "\/job-types\/4",
        "name": "DTP",
        "is_archived": false,
        "updated_on": 1430164436,
        "is_default": false,
        "default_hourly_rate": 150
    }
}
```

## Archived Job Types

Our example company recently got out of production of printed material, so we need to archive DTP job type. It's easy as:

**`PUT /move-to-archive/job-type/4`** → HTTP 200

Respuesta:
```json
{
    "single": {
        "id": 4,
        "class": "JobType",
        "url_path": "\/job-types\/4",
        "name": "DTP",
        "is_archived": true,
        "updated_on": 1430164436,
        "is_default": false,
        "default_hourly_rate": 150
    }
}
```

Archived job types are saved for the reference and can't be used for new time records:

## Default Job Type

System offers you a way to specify a default job type. This job type is pre-selected by default in time tracking forms (unless user has specified job type in their user profile). When ActiveCollab is installed, first job type is set as default:

**`GET /job-types/default`** → HTTP 200

Respuesta:
```json
{
    "single": {
        "id": 1,
        "class": "JobType",
        "url_path": "\/job-types\/1",
        "name": "Programming",
        "is_archived": false,
        "updated_on": 1430164435,
        "is_default": true,
        "default_hourly_rate": 150
    }
}
```

Lets make `Design` our default job type:

**`PUT /job-types/default`** → HTTP 200

Payload:
```json
{
    "job_type_id": 2
}
```

Respuesta:
```json
{
    "single": {
        "id": 2,
        "class": "JobType",
        "url_path": "\/job-types\/2",
        "name": "Design",
        "is_archived": false,
        "updated_on": 1430164435,
        "is_default": true,
        "default_hourly_rate": 120
    }
}
```

Archived job types can't be made default:

**`PUT /job-types/default`** → HTTP 500

Payload:
```json
{
    "job_type_id": 4
}
```

Respuesta:
```json
{
    "type": "InvalidParamError",
    "message": "Archived job types cannot be set as default",
    "file": "\/var\/www\/activecollab.back\/activecollab\/current\/modules\/tracking\/models\/job_types\/JobTypes.class.php",
    "line": 198,
    "trace": "#0 \/var\/www\/activecollab.back\/activecollab\/current\/modules\/tracking\/controllers\/JobTypesController.class.php(109): JobTypes::setDefault(Object(JobType))\n#1 \/var\/www\/angie.back\/src\/Angie\/Controller.php(42): JobTypesController->set_default(Object(Owner))\n#2 \/var\/www\/angie.back\/classes\/application\/AngieApplicationAdapter.class.php(243): Angie\\Controller->executeAction('set_default')\n#3 \/var\/www\/angie.back\/classes\/application\/AngieApplication.class.php(839): AngieApplicationAdapter->handleHttpRequest('job-types\/defau...', '')\n#4 \/var\/www\/activecollab.back\/instance\/public\/api.php(19): AngieApplication::handleHttpRequest()\n#5 {main}",
    "previous": null,
    "var_name": "job_type",
    "var_value": {
        "id": 4,
        "class": "JobType",
        "url_path": "\/job-types\/4",
        "name": "DTP",
        "is_archived": true,
        "updated_on": 1430164436,
        "is_default": false,
        "default_hourly_rate": 150
    }
}
```

## Deleting Job Types

Job types that are used by time records can't be deleted. Instead, consider archiving them if you no longer need them:

**`DELETE /job-types/1`** → HTTP 404

Default job type can't be deleted as well:

**`DELETE /job-types/2`** → HTTP 404

Unused job types can be deleted:

**`DELETE /job-types/3`** → HTTP 200

# Visibility

> Fuente: https://developers.activecollab.com/api-documentation/v1/projects/elements/time-records/visibility.html

Personas in this Story: Default, ProjectLeader, Member, Subcontractor, Client.

This article covers visibility of time records. In broad strokes:

1. Only owners and project leader always see all time records in a project,
2. Members and sucontractors see only their records,
3. Client see time records only if they were given permission to access tracked time and budget information.

pages.title: Labels
pages.markdown:
# Labels

> Fuente: https://developers.activecollab.com/api-documentation/v1/projects/labels.html

activeCollab ships with a couple of predefined project labels:

**`GET /labels/project-labels`** → HTTP 200

Respuesta:
```json
[
    {
        "id": 1,
        "class": "ProjectLabel",
        "url_path": "\/labels\/1",
        "name": "NEW",
        "updated_on": null,
        "color": "#FFFF00",
        "is_default": false,
        "position": 1
    },
    {
        "id": 2,
        "class": "ProjectLabel",
        "url_path": "\/labels\/2",
        "name": "INPROGRESS",
        "updated_on": null,
        "color": "#00A651",
        "is_default": false,
        "position": 2
    },
    {
        "id": 3,
        "class": "ProjectLabel",
        "url_path": "\/labels\/3",
        "name": "CANCELED",
        "updated_on": null,
        "color": "#FF0000",
        "is_default": false,
        "position": 3
... (12 líneas más)
```

For the sake of this test, lets assume that company who is useding the system does not find these defaults good for their workflow, and that they would like to implement something like this for their projects:

IDEA -> CONFIRMED or CANCELED -> INPROGRESS or PAUSED -> DONE or CANCELED

What we need to do is:

1. Rename a NEW label to IDEA
2. Add CONFRIEMD and DONE labels
3. Reorder labels so they are in the sequence that works for the proposed workflow:

- IDEA (1)
- CONFIRMED (will be 16)
- INPROGRESS (2)
- PAUSED (4)
- DONE (will be 17)
- CANCELED (3)

Lets start by renaming an existing label:

**`PUT /labels/1`** → HTTP 200

Payload:
```json
{
    "name": "Idea"
}
```

Respuesta:
```json
{
    "single": {
        "id": 1,
        "class": "ProjectLabel",
        "url_path": "\/labels\/1",
        "name": "IDEA",
        "updated_on": 1430164484,
        "color": "#FFFF00",
        "is_default": false,
        "position": 1
    }
}
```

Now, we need to add the new labels:

**`POST /labels`** → HTTP 200

Payload:
```json
{
    "type": "ProjectLabel",
    "name": "Confirmed"
}
```

Respuesta:
```json
{
    "single": {
        "id": 16,
        "class": "ProjectLabel",
        "url_path": "\/labels\/16",
        "name": "CONFIRMED",
        "updated_on": 1430164484,
        "color": null,
        "is_default": false,
        "position": 5
    }
}
```

**`POST /labels`** → HTTP 200

Payload:
```json
{
    "type": "ProjectLabel",
    "name": "Done"
}
```

Respuesta:
```json
{
    "single": {
        "id": 17,
        "class": "ProjectLabel",
        "url_path": "\/labels\/17",
        "name": "DONE",
        "updated_on": 1430164484,
        "color": null,
        "is_default": false,
```

pages.title: Announce
pages.markdown:
# Announce

> Fuente: https://developers.activecollab.com/api-documentation/v1/utilities/announce.html

Personas in this Story: Default, Member, Client.

ActiveCollab lets owners and technical administrators send out announcements to users. This feature is useful when you need to announce maintenance periods, some important achievements etc.

In order to see how this feature works, we have invited two users - one regular member and one technical administrator (owner has been automatically created when we installed ActiveCollab):

**`GET /users`** → HTTP 200

Respuesta:
```json
[
    {
        "id": 1,
        "class": "Owner",
        "url_path": "\/users\/1",
        "is_archived": false,
        "is_trashed": false,
        "trashed_on": null,
        "trashed_by_id": 0,
        "created_on": 1430164878,
        "created_by_id": 1,
        "updated_on": 1430164878,
        "updated_by_id": 1,
        "language_id": 0,
        "first_name": "Ilija.studen",
        "last_name": null,
        "display_name": "ilija.studen",
        "short_display_name": "ilija.studen",
        "email": "ilija.studen@activecollab.com",
        "additional_email_addresses": [],
        "is_pending_activation": false,
        "avatar_url": "http:\/\/feather.dev\/proxy.php?proxy=avatar&module=system&v=current&b=DEV&user_id=1&size=--SIZE--&timestamp=1430164878",
        "custom_permissions": [],
        "company_id": 1,
        "title": null,
        "phone": null,
        "im_type": null,
        "im_handle": null,
        "note": null
    },
... (119 líneas más)
```

When we try to send out an announcement as a member, system will reject our request:

**`POST /announce`** → HTTP 404 _(como Member)_

Payload:
```json
{
    "subject": "Hohoho!",
    "announcement": "We wish you a merry christmas",
    "recipients": "user1@activecollab.com, user2@activecollab.com"
}
```

If we try to make the same request as technical administrator, or as an owner, system will make no objection and it will send out the announcement to the listed people:

**`POST /announce`** → HTTP 500 _(como TechAdministrator)_

Payload:
```json
{
    "subject": "Hohoho!",
    "announcement": "We wish you a Merry Christmas",
    "recipients": "user1@activecollab.com, user2@activecollab.com"
}
```

**`POST /announce`** → HTTP 200

Payload:
```json
{
    "subject": "Hohoho!",
    "announcement": "We wish you a Merry Christmas",
    "recipients": "user1@activecollab.com, user2@activecollab.com"
}
```

Note about recipients: you should send them in standard RFC 822 format. You can send an announcement to up to 100 recipients per request. If you need more than that, please email support@activecollab.com for details.

pages.title: Compare Text
pages.markdown:
# Compare Text > Fuente: https://developers.activecollab.com/api-documentation/v1/utilities/compare-text.html If you need to compare two texts in your interface, ActiveCollab offers a simple way to achieve that without implementing another diff tool: **`POST /compare-text`** → HTTP 200 Payload: ```json { "before": "Diff is using character granularity", "after": "Diff is using word granularity" } ``` Respuesta: ```json { "before": "Diff is using character granularity", "after": "Diff is using word granularity", "diff": "Diff is using character <\/del>word <\/ins>granularity" } ``` Please note that HTML will be converted to plain text representation and than compared. Diff result is always HTML: **`POST /compare-text`** → HTTP 200 Payload: ```json { "before": "

The quick brown fox<\/p>

jumps<\/b> over the lazy dog<\/p>", "after": "

The quick grey elephant<\/p>

jumps over the busy snake<\/p>" } ``` Respuesta: ```json { "before": "The quick brown fox\n\nJUMPS over the lazy dog", "after": "The quick grey elephant\n\njumps over the busy snake", "diff": "The quick brown fox
\n
\nJUMPS <\/del>grey elephant
\n
\njumps <\/ins>over the lazy dog<\/del>busy snake<\/ins>" } ```

# Days Off

> Fuente: https://developers.activecollab.com/api-documentation/v1/utilities/days-off.html

System starts with no off days defined:

**`GET /day-offs`** → HTTP 200

Respuesta:
```json
[]
```

But we can add single or multi day events:

**`POST /day-offs`** → HTTP 200

Payload:
```json
{
    "name": "Christmas",
    "start_date": "2014-12-25",
    "end_date": "2014-12-25",
    "repeat_yearly": true
}
```

Respuesta:
```json
{
    "single": {
        "id": 1,
        "class": "DayOff",
        "url_path": "\/day-offs\/1",
        "name": "Christmas",
        "start_date": 1419465600,
        "end_date": 1419465600,
        "is_multi_day": false,
        "repeat_yearly": true
    }
}
```

**`POST /day-offs`** → HTTP 200

Payload:
```json
{
    "name": "My 1st",
    "start_date": "2014-05-01",
    "end_date": "2014-05-03",
    "repeat_yearly": true
}
```

Respuesta:

```json
        "end_date": 1399075200,
        "is_multi_day": true,
        "repeat_yearly": true
    }
}
```

To update a record, simply send a PUT request, like we did in case of the spelling error for the second event that we added:

**`PUT /day-offs/2`** → HTTP 200

```json
{

}
```

Respuesta:

```json
        "url_path": "\/day-offs\/2",

        "end_date": 1399075200,
        "is_multi_day": true,
        "repeat_yearly": true
```

Now we can check `/day-offs` collection:

**`GET /day-offs`** → HTTP 200

**`DELETE /day-offs/2`** → HTTP 200

```json
    ]
]
```

To clear subscribers, we should send DELETE command:

**`DELETE /subscribers/task/1`** → HTTP 200

```json
[]
```

```json
]
```

Respuesta:
```json
[
    2
]
```
